# API Reference

Signatures and complete docstrings for every public symbol in `pllm`, grouped by task. For narrative usage guides and runnable examples, see the [User Guides](../README.md#user-guides).

<!-- api: generated by tools/check_docs.py --write-generated; do not edit -->
## Engine & Workloads

### `pllm.make_llm`

```text
pllm.make_llm(config: 'ModelConfig', *, workload: 'Workload | None' = None) -> 'VllmLlm'
```

A context-managed vLLM engine; execution options apply when a workload is installed.

### `pllm.make_async_llm`

```text
pllm.make_async_llm(config: 'ModelConfig', *, workload: 'Workload | None' = None) -> 'AsyncVllmLlm'
```

An async continuous-batching vLLM engine handle (`async with make_async_llm(...) as llm:`).

### `pllm.explain`

```text
pllm.explain(workload: 'Workload', config: 'ModelConfig') -> 'ExplainResult'
```

Plan using model/quantization metadata and shape-only tracing; never load weights or allocate CUDA storage.

Declared pretrained state files are read and validated on CPU.

Memory excludes base-model weights, KV cache and vLLM model-graph/activation pools. GPU fit is decided by make_llm.
A too-small declared execution/state budget returns the unrestricted plan with actionable budget_errors.

### `pllm.Workload`

```text
pllm.Workload()
```

Python methods and effects compiled once, with independent sub-workloads in dataclass fields.

Sampler additions follow member declaration order (parent methods, then fields recursively), before
vLLM filters and at most one guide. Set required_publish_lag when the algorithm requires a fixed
value; every component must agree with the engine's ExecutionOptions.publish_lag.

### `pllm.ModelConfig`

```text
pllm.ModelConfig(model: str, dtype: Literal['bfloat16', 'float16', 'float32'] = 'bfloat16', max_model_len: int = 512, max_num_seqs: int = 8, max_num_batched_tokens: int = 512, gpu_memory_utilization: float = 0.5, kv_cache_memory_bytes: int | None = None, seed: int = 0, trust_remote_code: bool = False, enable_prefix_caching: bool = False, enable_chunked_prefill: bool = False, generated_kv: Literal['reuse', 'isolate'] = 'isolate', revision: str | None = None, multiprocessing: Union[Literal['auto'], bool] = 'auto', execution: pllm.config.ExecutionOptions = ..., cuda_graphs: Union[Literal['auto'], bool] = 'auto', kv_offload: pllm.config.KVOffload | None = None, tensor_parallel_size: int = 1, pipeline_parallel_size: int = 1, data_parallel_size: int = 1)
```

### `pllm.ExecutionOptions`

```text
pllm.ExecutionOptions(max_host_training_rows: int = 1, cuda_graph_pool_budget_bytes: int | None = None, state_page_budget_bytes: int = 0, execution_peak_budget_bytes: int | None = None, allow_numerical_transforms: bool = True, tuning: Literal['heuristic', 'measured'] = 'heuristic', publish_lag: int = 1, guidance_capacity: int | None = 4096)
```

Framework execution policy; lag counts post-sampler steps hidden from readers.

Post-filter guidance defaults to capacity K=4096. Choose capacities so the common
case never takes the overflow path; smaller K is slower because overflow rows need
top-K selection. In the measured ESamp beta=.5 corpus, the largest real nucleus was
2,785 tokens, so K=4096 kept those rows on the simple path; throughput per capacity is
recorded in doc/reference/measurements.toml. Other workloads may not fit the capacity.

Capture pools are automatic unless cuda_graph_pool_budget_bytes sets a cap.
Tensor tasks reserve their traced requirements; vLLM owns its model-graph pool,
whose measured allocation is checked against an explicit cap after capture.
explain reports task funding and excludes vLLM model-graph/activation pools.

### `pllm.KVOffload`

```text
pllm.KVOffload(connector: Literal['OffloadingConnector', 'SimpleCPUOffloadConnector'] = 'OffloadingConnector', cpu_bytes: int = 536870912, prompt_only: bool = False)
```

Batched same-engine CPU offload of complete allocation pages.

## Reading Model Internals: Input Markers

### `pllm.hidden`

```text
pllm.hidden(layer: 'int | Callable[[Any], int]' = 0, *, tokens: "Literal['decode', 'prefill', 'all']" = 'decode') -> 'Any'
```

The MLP output before the residual add in decoder layer `layer` (negative from the end).

One row per request: the latest decode token, or with tokens="prefill" the last prompt token of completed prefill.
tokens="all" reads one row per token the step computes, prompt chunks included, in token order within each
request; tokens a preempted request recomputes are read once. Only @pllm.export methods read these rows: each
step can carry max_num_batched_tokens of them, so give the export max_rows that large (pllm.explain reports the
host copy volume).

### `pllm.residual`

```text
pllm.residual(layer: 'int | Callable[[Any], int]', *, after: "Literal['layer', 'attention']" = 'layer', tokens: "Literal['decode', 'prefill', 'all']" = 'decode') -> 'Any'
```

The residual stream after decoder layer `layer` (negative from the end): the embedding plus every earlier
sublayer's output, which the next sublayer normalizes. This is what steering vectors, sparse autoencoders and the
logit lens read; pllm.hidden(layer) is only the layer's MLP output before it is added to this stream.
after="attention" reads the stream between the layer's attention and its MLP. Rows are chosen by `tokens` as in
pllm.hidden.

### `pllm.final_hidden`

```text
pllm.final_hidden(*, tokens: "Literal['decode', 'prefill', 'all']" = 'decode') -> 'Any'
```

The hidden state after the model's final norm, which the LM head reads (Hugging Face's last_hidden_state);
rows are chosen by `tokens` as in pllm.hidden.

### `pllm.layer_logits`

```text
pllm.layer_logits(layers: 'tuple[int, ...] | Callable[[Any], tuple[int, ...]]') -> 'Any'
```

The model's final norm and LM head applied to the residual stream after each of `layers` (negative from the
end), as float32 [rows, len(layers), vocab]: the logit lens. The last layer's logits are the model's own. One row
for each token the sampler draws: a prompt's last token and every decode token.

### `pllm.attention`

```text
pllm.attention(layer: 'int', fact: 'Fact') -> 'Any'
```

Read sampled attention aux or the first kv.attend call's float32 LSE; inside attention, use earlier layers.

### `pllm.input_tokens`

```text
pllm.input_tokens(*, history: 'int' = 0) -> 'Any'
```

Int64 [rows, history + 1] token ids: current token first, then lookbacks; -1 before the request starts.

Results consumed by custom_residual use every scheduled token; other methods use sampled rows.

### `pllm.sample_index`

```text
pllm.sample_index(limit: 'int | Callable[[Any], int] | None' = None) -> 'Any'
```

The sample index of each row's request: 0 for a prompt's first sample.

With `limit`, generate rejects requests whose sample index is `limit` or more.

### `pllm.base_logits`

```text
pllm.base_logits() -> 'Any'
```

The model's logits before any workload adjustment.

### `pllm.sampled_tokens`

```text
pllm.sampled_tokens() -> 'Any'
```

The tokens the sampler drew this step.

### `pllm.result`

```text
pllm.result(operation: 'str') -> 'Any'
```

The value another operation of this workload returned in the same step.

### `pllm.parameter`

```text
pllm.parameter(state: 'str', field: 'str', *, per_row: 'bool' = False) -> 'Any'
```

One tensor field of a declared state, aligned to the operation's rows for request state.

### `pllm.module`

```text
pllm.module(state: 'str') -> 'Any'
```

A state declared with init=pllm.FromModule(...), called like the module; request state uses each row's own
parameters.

### `pllm.version`

```text
pllm.version(state: 'str') -> 'Any'
```

How many updates each row's state has received (0 before the first update).

### `pllm.index`

```text
pllm.index(state: 'str') -> 'Any'
```

Each row's slot in the state pool, for indexing pooled tensors.

### `pllm.carry`

```text
pllm.carry(source: 'InputMarker', *, state: 'str', field: 'str') -> 'Any'
```

Read `source` and, when the training update publishes, write its value into the carried `state.field`.

The next step reads that field as its input version; per request the last selected row wins.

### `pllm.depth`

```text
pllm.depth() -> 'Any'
```

Inside a @pllm.custom_residual method, the index of the place it runs at, a Python int: the layer, or
2 * layer (+ 1 for the MLP) with site="both".

### `pllm.value`

```text
pllm.value(layer: 'int | Callable[[Any], int]') -> 'Any'
```

Inside a @pllm.custom_residual method, the value rows [rows, kv_heads, head_dim] layer `layer` computed for the
same token in this forward (after its own value rewrite).

### `pllm.operand`

```text
pllm.operand(name: 'OperandName | Callable[[Any], OperandName]') -> 'Any'
```

A projection input/target/weight, input token embedding, or scalar prompt-end bool.

Embeddings are the residual stream entering the first decoder layer, before its input norm, aligned with each
projection row.

### `pllm.batch`

```text
pllm.batch(field: "Literal['hidden', 'base_logits', 'labels', 'weights', 'targets', 'input_ids', 'attention_mask']") -> 'Any'
```

One field of the host batch passed to generate.

The fields a @pllm.train method reads pick its batch: WeightedRowBatch (hidden, targets, weights) or
CausalTrainBatch (input_ids, labels, attention_mask, weights) take one AdamW step;
WeightedCEBatch (hidden, base_logits, labels, weights) runs SGD steps per state.

### `pllm.causal_model`

```text
pllm.causal_model(adapter: 'str') -> 'Any'
```

The causal LM with the named pllm.model.Adapter applied, as a pllm.model.CausalModel; .base skips it.

## Owning State: Scopes, Initializers & Optimizers

### `pllm.RequestState`

```text
pllm.RequestState(fields: 'Mapping[str, Shape | Field]' = <factory>, shape: 'Shape | None' = None, dtype: "torch.dtype | Literal['auto']" = 'auto', key_fields: 'tuple[KeyField, ...]' = ('request_id',), *, init: 'StateInit' = Zeros(), optimizer: 'AdamWConfig | SGD | None' = None, alignment: 'int' = 16, carry: 'Mapping[str, Shape]' = <factory>, layers: 'tuple[int, ...]' = ())
```

Per-request parameters, read as tensors aligned to the current operation's rows.

### `pllm.InstanceState`

```text
pllm.InstanceState(fields: 'Mapping[str, Shape | Field]' = <factory>, shape: 'Shape | None' = None, dtype: "torch.dtype | Literal['auto']" = 'auto', *, init: 'StateInit' = Zeros(), optimizer: 'AdamWConfig | SGD | None' = None, alignment: 'int' = 16, carry: 'Mapping[str, Shape]' = <factory>, layers: 'tuple[int, ...]' = ())
```

State shared by requests. `init` says where its starting values come from (default pllm.Zeros()):
pllm.Computed(function), pllm.Pretrained(path), pllm.ModelCheckpoint(names), pllm.FromModule(factory),
pllm.Fed(order) or pllm.Imported(). Values convert to the declared storage dtype, including trainable states.

### `pllm.PositionState`

```text
pllm.PositionState(initial: float = 0.0)
```

One model-hidden vector per KV allocation block, initialized at token zero.

### `pllm.Field`

```text
pllm.Field(shape: 'tuple[int, ...] | Callable[[int, int], tuple[int, ...]]', dtype: "torch.dtype | Literal['auto']" = 'auto')
```

A state field with an explicit dtype, or a shape computed from a projection's (in_features, out_features);
a field read by an adapter gets one copy per target projection. Without a dtype it takes its state's dtype=;
with neither, storage follows the declared role: accumulators use FP32, other fields use model precision.

### `pllm.Dimensions`

```text
pllm.Dimensions(hidden_size: 'int', vocab_size: 'int', targets: 'tuple[ProjectionShape, ...]' = (), dtype: 'TensorDType' = <TensorDType.FLOAT32: 'float32'>, layer_count: 'int' = 0, tensor_parallel_size: 'int' = 1)
```

Global model widths for workload declarations, and the probed shape of every projection the workload's
adapters and @pllm.train_in_forward target.

### `pllm.Zeros`

```text
pllm.Zeros()
```

Every field starts at zero (the default).

### `pllm.Computed`

```text
pllm.Computed(function: 'Initializer')
```

`function(fields, generator)` fills the named field tensors in place, once per build with a seeded
generator; every admission copies the result.

### `pllm.Pretrained`

```text
pllm.Pretrained(path: 'str', placement: "Literal['device', 'host']" = 'device')
```

Tensors from a safetensors file: a plain state loads the tensors named like its fields, a module state
(pllm.FromModule(..., pretrained=path)) a strict state_dict. Values convert to the declared storage dtype.

placement="host" keeps a read-only table of gathered fields in pinned host memory; "device" (default) never
falls back to host. Budgets count device residency separately.

### `pllm.ModelCheckpoint`

```text
pllm.ModelCheckpoint(names: 'Mapping[str, str]')
```

Tensors of the served model's own checkpoint, one name per field (with `layers=`, a pattern formatted with
each `{layer}`); vLLM skips them when it loads the model. The state is read-only.

### `pllm.FromModule`

```text
pllm.FromModule(factory: 'ModuleFactory', pretrained: 'str' = '')
```

The parameters of an `nn.Module` built from the model's dimensions become the state's one field, initialized as
the module initializes them, or from a safetensors state_dict at `pretrained`. pllm.module(state) calls it.

### `pllm.Fed`

```text
pllm.Fed(order: "Literal['ordered', 'latest']")
```

Filled by a producer process (VllmLlm.feed): "ordered" consumes every publication in order, "latest" only the
newest. A workload declares at most one fed state.

### `pllm.Imported`

```text
pllm.Imported()
```

Supplied by generate(batch=pllm.io.StateImport(...)) and applied before the request's first forward: one row
per prompt for a RequestState, the field tensors for an InstanceState.

### `pllm.AdamW`

```text
pllm.AdamW(lr: 'float', betas: 'tuple[float, float]' = (0.9, 0.999), eps: 'float' = 1e-08, weight_decay: 'float' = 0.0)
```

### `pllm.SGD`

```text
pllm.SGD(lr: 'float')
```

## Routing Outputs: Effects & Phases

### `pllm.export`

```text
pllm.export(*, name: 'str | Callable[[Any], str]' = 'value', every: 'int | Callable[[Any], int]' = 1, max_rows: 'int | Callable[[Any], int]' = 1, max_cols: 'int | Callable[[Any], int]' = 16, enabled: 'bool | Callable[[Any], bool]' = True, overflow: "Literal['drop', 'block']" = 'drop') -> 'Callable[[F], F]'
```

Deliver bounded observations of executed forward rows to on_export.

A step delivers at most max_rows rows, split into events of whole rows of at most 32 KiB; each event lists
every row's request identity and token position. Async scheduling can execute one extra decode row before
learning that a request stopped at EOS; that row is observed too. Callbacks run asynchronously and close()
drains their delivery. Block on a full export queue only when explicitly requested.

### `pllm.add_logits`

```text
pllm.add_logits(*, rows: 'str' = '') -> 'Callable[[F], F]'
```

Add the returned tensor to the logits before sampling.

`rows` (here and on the other effects) names a method returning a boolean mask: only those rows run.

### `pllm.guide_sampling`

```text
pllm.guide_sampling(*, beta: 'float | Callable[[Any], float]', rows: 'str' = '') -> 'Callable[[F], F]'
```

Push sampling away from the returned hidden-state prediction for positive `beta`.

On finite top-k/top-p survivors, use `(1 + beta) * logits - beta * pred_logits`, where the model's LM head
projects the returned hidden states to `pred_logits`.

### `pllm.write`

```text
pllm.write(*, state: 'str', fields: 'tuple[str, ...]') -> 'Callable[[F], F]'
```

Atomically publish a tuple of computed fields; request values have a leading request axis.

### `pllm.train`

```text
pllm.train(*, state: 'str', update_rows: 'str' = '', reduction: 'TrainReduction' = 'mean', steps: 'int | Callable[[Any], int]' = 1, reset: 'str' = '', rows: 'str' = '') -> 'Callable[[F], F]'
```

Minimize the returned loss with `state`'s optimizer; updates publish after sampling by default.

With tensor parallelism, independent automatic request training can compute a private update before the
draw. Publication still follows sampling; cancellation discards the private version. Use
`@pllm.on(pllm.Phase.AFTER_SAMPLE)` to require the computation itself to follow sampling.

The method's inputs say what it trains on. Without pllm.batch fields it trains each request's state on that
request's rows (pllm.AdamW). WeightedRowBatch or CausalTrainBatch fields, or a causal model, take one AdamW
step on the host batch. WeightedCEBatch fields run `steps` SGD steps per state, each state first restored by
the `reset` method (pllm.SGD).

Request-row methods return a [rows] loss. The default `reduction="mean"` averages each state's selected
rows in this engine step; `"sum"` sums them. Both keep states independent. Each state takes one optimizer
step per engine step; prompt rows train once per prefill chunk, so prompt training depends on chunking.
Reduction matters for prompt rows, shared key_fields states, InstanceState, or any step with several rows
per state. Plain request_id decode training has one row per state, so both reductions are equal.
Choose mean for AdamW by default; choose sum for a per-token SGD learning rate or shared-key online group
training, where each surviving token should contribute without division by the group's current row count.

Host-batch methods return one scalar and own their reduction; a non-default reduction= is rejected.
`rows=` names a selector whose mask picks the rows that count; zero-weight losses still count toward the
mean, and the method still runs on every row. The selector runs on the method's rows, at its tokens= phase,
whatever the selector itself reads. For request training, rows= and update_rows= require a model
effect without sampler guidance, or @pllm.add_logits; standalone training and @pllm.guide_sampling update
every selected state.

### `pllm.differentiate`

```text
pllm.differentiate(*, inputs: 'tuple[str, ...]' = (), parameters: 'bool' = False, input_rows: 'str' = '', parameter_rows: 'str' = '') -> 'Callable[[F], F]'
```

Keep derivative edges; parameters may stay frozen while inputs differentiate.

### `pllm.UpdateOutput`

```text
pllm.UpdateOutput(output: 'torch.Tensor', changed: 'torch.Tensor', update_count: 'torch.Tensor', trained_rows: 'torch.Tensor', metrics: 'Mapping[str, torch.Tensor]' = <factory>)
```

What a training or overlay method returns: its output and 0-d device counters.

`output` is the loss for `@pllm.train` methods; for `@pllm.train_in_forward` it is the unscaled residual
the overlay adds, excluding the base projection. `changed` (bool) says whether state changed,
`update_count` (int64) counts applied updates and `trained_rows` (int64) the rows that trained.
All three are 0-d tensors on the output's device, never Python scalars, so the step needs no host sync.
`metrics` are extra 0-d device tensors returned in the step result.

### `pllm.on`

```text
pllm.on(phase: 'Phase | Callable[[Any], Phase]') -> 'Callable[[F], F]'
```

Run the method in `phase`; needed for methods without an effect or to move an effect's phase.

### `pllm.Phase`

```text
pllm.Phase: BEFORE_FORWARD | AFTER_FORWARD | BEFORE_SAMPLE | AFTER_SAMPLE | IN_FORWARD | AUTOMATIC
```

The windows of one engine step a method can run in (@pllm.on); each effect has a default window.

### `pllm.cfg`

```text
pllm.cfg(path: 'str') -> 'Any'
```

Refer to a workload attribute or dotted path in a decorator or marker setting.

## Editing Model Sites & Forward Loops

### `pllm.model.ActivationPatch`

```text
pllm.model.ActivationPatch(state: 'str', layers: 'tuple[int, ...]', first_tokens: 'int' = 0, last_tokens: 'int' = 2, operator: "Literal['low_rank_affine', 'add']" = 'low_rank_affine', *, decode: 'bool' = False, refresh: "Literal['admission', 'step']" = 'admission', on_missing: "Literal['stop', 'hold']" = 'stop')
```

Edit the hidden state at `layers` from a state, whoever writes it (ReFT-style): the first and last prompt
tokens, and with decode=True every decode token.

operator="low_rank_affine" reads three fields per layer, "add" one delta per layer. refresh="admission" keeps
the version a request was admitted with; "step" reads the newest version at every decode step, and on_missing
says what a step without a new version does ("stop" the request or "hold" the last version).

### `pllm.model.Adapter`

```text
pllm.model.Adapter(state: 'str', targets: 'tuple[Projection, ...]', weight: 'str' = 'value', operator: 'AdapterOperator' = 'dense', factors: 'tuple[str, str]' = ('a', 'b'), scale: 'float' = 1.0)
```

Apply a state as a weight delta at the target projections, whoever trains it (a PEFT-style adapter).

`weight` names the field of a "dense" or "per_head" delta, `factors` the two fields of a "low_rank" one; the
delta is multiplied by `scale`.

A weight delta applies on every invocation of its projection, including repeated layer calls and replay in
@pllm.custom_forward. Each call uses its actual input and each row's request state, pinned at forward entry.
Compacted active= rows and reordered waves retain that ownership through device indices; skipped projections
receive no correction. Native QKV propagation for skipped layers still applies the Q/V deltas when it runs.
This lets custom depth schedules use the same adapted model as the standard forward.

At TP>1 (vLLM 0.32), dense and low_rank deltas follow each projection's shards.
Declare fields with Field(lambda inputs, outputs: ...). Down deltas partition dense weights and A
by input columns, with replicated B. Attention q/k/v and MLP gate/up deltas partition dense weights and B
by output rows, with replicated A; KV head replicas follow vLLM's head placement. Small fields replicate.
Initialization runs globally before slicing, and explain reports per-rank storage. vLLM's existing row
reduction sums corrected down partials; no extra collective is added. Updates must be shard-local: training
replicated A from column-sharded outputs, or B from row-sharded inputs, requires tensor_parallel_size=1.
Sharded fields are read only in projection transitions; replicated factors remain available to other methods.
TP updates reject captured tensor constants; use Python scalars, new_full/new_ones or replicated state fields.
per_head deltas, imported/checkpoint adapters and side-lane adapter training still require TP=1.

### `pllm.model.Projection`

```text
pllm.model.Projection(name: 'ProjectionName', layer: 'int | None' = None)
```

One linear projection of the base model by its Hugging Face module name; `layer=None` means every layer.

### `pllm.model.LayerRoute`

```text
pllm.model.LayerRoute(state: 'str', *, over: 'tuple[int, ...]', field: 'str' = 'layer')
```

Route hidden reads, residual patches or homogeneous projection adapters by an int64 state field.

`over` names the explicit candidate layers installed into the model graph; negative indices resolve from the end
at bind time. At runtime, the scalar int64 field `state.field` selects one physical layer index in `0..layers-1`,
or `-1` to disable the route for that row/step without recapturing CUDA graphs. Derived reads, `patch(decode=True)`
and `adapter(...)` default to `refresh="step"` (Forward-only KV; `patch(decode=False)` defaults to `refresh="admission"`).

### `pllm.train_in_forward`

```text
pllm.train_in_forward(*, state: 'str', targets: 'tuple[Projection, ...] | Callable[[Any], tuple[Projection, ...]]', weight: 'str' = 'value', operator: 'AdapterOperator | Callable[[Any], AdapterOperator]' = 'dense', factors: 'tuple[str, str] | Callable[[Any], tuple[str, str]]' = ('a', 'b'), scale: 'float | Callable[[Any], float]' = 1.0, tokens: 'Tokens | Callable[[Any], Tokens]' = 'prefill', visibility: 'VisibilityKind | Callable[[Any], VisibilityKind]' = 'forward_pinned', chunk: 'int | Callable[[Any], int] | None' = None, flush: "Literal['prompt_end'] | None" = None) -> 'Callable[[F], F]'
```

Train a request state inside the forward and add its residual at each target projection.

`tokens` picks the tokens whose projection operands train the state: "prefill", "decode" or "all";
`operator`, `weight`, `factors` and `scale` say how the state changes each projection, as in
pllm.model.Adapter. visibility="forward_pinned" reads the state the forward started with; "exact" also reads
every chunk already trained in this forward. Column projections expose their replicated input as
operand("target"); readouts have the projection's output width, which can differ from that input width.
At TP>1, state initialization and shard-local update rules are the same as pllm.model.Adapter.

With ``chunk``, the function takes the weight carry followed by input/target/embedding row operands and returns
(next carry, readouts). Pending rows belong to the framework. When ``state`` declares
``optimizer=pllm.SGD(lr)``, return one loss per row instead; gradients accumulate until a chunk completes,
including a short final chunk with ``flush="prompt_end"``.

### `pllm.custom_residual`

```text
pllm.custom_residual(*, site: 'Site', layers: 'tuple[int, ...] | Callable[[Any], tuple[int, ...]] | None' = None, read: 'str' = '', streams: 'int | Callable[[Any], int]' = 1, state: 'str' = '', chunk: 'int | Callable[[Any], int] | None' = None) -> 'Callable[[F], F]'
```

Own the residual update at `site` of `layers` (default: every layer) with this method.

site="attention" or "mlp" (or "both", in forward order) take the stream before the sublayer and its branch
output, `write(x, y, ...) -> stream`, replacing the plain `x + y`; the native branch always runs. site="value"
maps a full-attention layer's value rows [rows, kv_heads, head_dim] before attention reads and caches them;
site="final" maps the stream entering the final norm to one stream. `read` names a method `(x, ...) -> branch
input` that the sublayer normalizes instead of the stream. With `streams=n` the stream is [rows, n, hidden] from the
embedding to a "final" method that collapses it. After the site tensors, methods read pllm.parameter, pllm.module,
pllm.depth(), pllm.value(layer) and pllm.residual(layer) (the same token, earlier in this forward). Tensors are in the
model dtype; compute in float32 inside the method when needed.

With `state` (a pllm.RequestState with one field) and `chunk`, the method is a stateful sublayer at one site: it
sees one chunk of one request, `write(x, y, carry=pllm.parameter(state, ...), ...) -> (stream, next carry)`,
where every row reads the carry its chunk started with and a chunk's update applies once its last row has run.
Each row's stream should depend only on that row and the carry.

### `pllm.custom_attention`

```text
pllm.custom_attention(*, layers: 'tuple[int, ...] | Callable[[Any], tuple[int, ...]] | None' = None, keep: 'Keep' = 'all', window: 'int | Callable[[Any], int]' = 0, source: 'int | Callable[[Any], int]' = 0, sink: 'bool | Callable[[Any], bool]' = False) -> 'Callable[[F], F]'
```

Replace dense FlashAttention reads, retaining native projections and KV writes.

The method receives post-RoPE q [rows, heads, head_dim] and pllm.model.PagedKV.
Return attention with q's shape/dtype, optionally paired with aux [rows, ...].
kv.attend returns (output, float32 LSE); window and per-head topk select reads
without freeing storage. Methods may call pure torch.library.custom_op kernels.
keep="window", window=N frees old blocks through vLLM's SlidingWindowSpec.
sink=True retains the entire prompt plus that window (vLLM RSWASpec).
keep="none", source=k allocates no cache and reads the layer k below.
Layouts restrict every read, including topk; window_start marks the retained tail.
Requires TP=1, unquantized FA2 attention and prefix caching disabled.
Static layouts cannot accompany PositionState or custom forwards.
The prompt-sink FA2 read uses a gathered FP32 softmax; storage and reclamation
are owned by vLLM's RSWAManager. Score-based memory eviction is unsupported.

### `pllm.model.PagedKV`

```text
pllm.model.PagedKV(key_cache: 'torch.Tensor', value_cache: 'torch.Tensor', block_table: 'torch.Tensor', seq_lens: 'torch.Tensor', query_start: 'torch.Tensor', query_count: 'int', read_attention: 'AttentionRead', storage_window: 'int' = 0, prompt_lens: 'torch.Tensor | None' = None, storage_kind: "Literal['kv', 'mla_latent']" = 'kv', latent_cache: 'torch.Tensor | None' = None, rope_cache: 'torch.Tensor | None' = None, w_uk_t: 'torch.Tensor | None' = None, w_uv: 'torch.Tensor | None' = None)
```

Borrowed paged K/V, already including the current tokens; never changes cache storage.

Dense pages have shape [blocks, block_size, kv_heads, head_dim]. MLA stores
[blocks, block_size, latent_rank] and [blocks, block_size, rope_dim] views,
with per-head [nope_dim, latent_rank] and [latent_rank, v_dim] projections.
``topk`` contains
logical token positions [rows, k] or [rows, query_heads, k], padded with -1.
Different heads and layers may select different budgets. Selection saves reads,
not allocated KV memory. ``window`` counts tokens including the current token.

### `pllm.custom_forward`

```text
pllm.custom_forward(*, tokens: 'Tokens' = 'all', over: 'Over' = 'token') -> 'Callable[[F], F]'
```

Replace the forward of the selected tokens with this method's program over model layer slices and tensor math.

``tokens`` follows the token's prompt/generated role, including after preemption.
``over="token"`` runs each position independently in causal order. ``over="span"``
packs each request's contiguous scheduled tokens into [M, H] hidden tensors;
position and generated flags have shape [M, 1]. Spans cannot load predecessors.
Inputs after layers use pllm.parameter / pllm.module to read InstanceState, shared
by every token; the method body reads plain settings from self.

### `pllm.model.Layers`

```text
pllm.model.Layers(embeddings: torch.Tensor, position: torch.Tensor, layer_count: int, generated: torch.Tensor, entries: dict[str, torch.Tensor], over: Literal['token', 'span'] = 'token', namespace: str = '')
```

Public model slices and position state used inside custom_forward methods.

### `pllm.model.LayerOutputs`

```text
pllm.model.LayerOutputs(values: tuple[torch.Tensor, ...], start: int, layer_count: int)
```

Post-layer residual streams indexed by absolute layer, negative from the model end.

### `pllm.scan`

```text
pllm.scan(step: collections.abc.Callable[..., tuple[torch.Tensor, torch.Tensor]], *, carry: torch.Tensor, over: tuple[torch.Tensor, ...], chunk: int, invariants: tuple[torch.Tensor, ...] = (), valid_rows: torch.Tensor | None = None) -> tuple[torch.Tensor, tuple[torch.Tensor, ...]]
```

Run ``step(carry, *slices, *invariants)`` in chunk order, returning exclusive readouts.

Counted calls advance carry only for complete chunks within the device row count;
inactive capacity still evaluates its readout. Strict, CPU, partial, aliased and
differentiable calls preserve source operation order. Step owners and closures
must be immutable; pass varying tensor values through explicit arguments.

## Contract & Equivalence Verification

### `pllm.testing.check`

```text
pllm.testing.check(workload: 'Workload', config: 'ModelConfig', *, neutral: 'Workload | None' = None) -> 'CheckResult'
```

Check fixed request schedules on CPU using config shapes and the real planner/executor.

Permutes rows, perturbs neighbors, mixes chunked prompts, and replays preempted histories.
Checks actual state versions against publish_lag; exact projection visibility uses chunk/replay equivalence.
ContractError lists discrepancies and identifies workload row mixing or framework routing.
Composites also compare each field component with its standalone outputs, bitwise.
Pass neutral= with disabled author settings to check zero additive logits, absent guidance and residual methods
that return the base residual; neutral model effects the CPU harness does not execute are reported as skips.
Model execution, host inputs and shared training exceptions are reported as explicit skips.

### `pllm.testing.check_on_gpu`

```text
pllm.testing.check_on_gpu(workload: 'Workload', config: 'ModelConfig', *, neutral: 'Workload | None' = None) -> 'CheckResult'
```

Load real engines to check planning, eight steady decode anchors, schedule independence and neutral sampling.

The reference is the workload itself: three prompts are generated one at a time, then together in reverse
order (chunked, prefill mixed with decode), then together again while vLLM's KV allocator fails once so a
request is evicted and recomputed. Every request's token IDs must match bitwise, its exports and terminal
request state within dtype tolerance (chunking and recompute reorder a request's own sums). Exact-decode
workloads also compare eager execution with the captured graphs. The check runs in a child process whose
engines use vLLM's batch-invariant kernels (VLLM_BATCH_INVARIANT=1); a crash there is reported as a failed
check with the child's output. Instance states written while generating and publish_lag reads make solo and
batched runs legitimately differ: that comparison is reported as a skip, as are declared replay rejections.
Neutral checks compare greedy and seeded token IDs bitwise when model kernels match vanilla.
Inductor model hooks can change fusion: those compare teacher-forced full-vocabulary distributions
on greedy and seeded continuations, with mean/P99 KL <= .001/.01 nats (both directions) and
mean/P99 TV <= .01/.05. Successful checks report the comparison and measured distances.
Causal batches also check that permuting sequences and weights preserves an AdamW update.
Workloads with custom ops replay CPU-script method and cell inputs on CUDA and compare outputs
with dtype-default tolerances. The fake decoder excludes model arithmetic from that comparison.
Needs a CUDA device; multiprocessing and parallel workers are unsupported. The child starts like a
multiprocessing "spawn" process, so a script that calls this at module level needs `if __name__ == "__main__":`.

### `pllm.testing.check_distribution`

```text
pllm.testing.check_distribution(workload: 'Workload', config: 'ModelConfig', *, prompts: 'Sequence[str] | None' = None, tokens: 'int' = 16, temperature: 'float' = 0, max_mean_kl: 'float | None' = None, max_p99_kl: 'float | None' = None, max_mean_tv: 'float | None' = None, max_p99_tv: 'float | None' = None, worst: 'int' = 5) -> 'DistributionResult'
```

Measure how far a workload moves the plain model's output distribution on CUDA.

A dense, cheap quality signal complements token equality: a workload can look
fine on average while breaking rare token positions. P99 exposes that tail; a mean alone can
hide it. This measures movement, not task quality, and only covers the supplied sequences.

The plain model generates `tokens` greedy (temperature=0) or seeded sampled continuation
tokens for each prompt (check_on_gpu's two sequence prompts by default). The workload then
teacher-forces those same tokens through vLLM's native sampler, including sampler feedback
and state updates. Prompts are prefills; measured predictions start at the prompt end and
cover the continuation, not every interior prompt position. Requests run one at a time so
both engines have identical batch geometry. Each prompt must fit max_num_batched_tokens,
and prompt + tokens must fit max_model_len. Both engines use the workload's checkpoint and
graph/compile settings, including eager fallback. Run in a fresh process; multiprocessing
and parallel workers are unsupported. Every engine is closed, including on failure.

Both KL directions (nats) and TV are reduced over the FULL vocabulary on device in FP32,
using torch log_softmax on native logits. Distances use temperature=1 with no top-k/top-p
truncation; `temperature` only selects the plain continuation. The workload's configured
bounded/dense guidance is preserved. Zero probability contributes zero to KL; support
removal can give infinite KL. No diagnostic host reads/syncs occur inside model steps;
synchronization happens at run boundaries and when fetching final summaries. Baseline
log probabilities stay on device (about prompts * tokens * vocabulary * 4 bytes).

Returns mean, nearest-rank P99, max and `worst` positions for each metric, plus timings.
Positions are (prompt_index, token_offset), zero-based in prompt + continuation, naming
the predicted token. max_mean_kl / max_p99_kl bound BOTH KL directions;
max_mean_tv / max_p99_tv bound total variation. With no thresholds
this is a measurement; supplied thresholds set result.passed and result.failures without
discarding the numbers or raising ContractError. NaN distances always fail.

### `pllm.testing.CheckResult`

```text
pllm.testing.CheckResult(passed: 'tuple[str, ...]', skipped: 'tuple[CheckSkip, ...]')
```

Verified properties and explicit skips; dataclasses.asdict produces JSON-ready data.

```text

```

### `pllm.testing.DistributionResult`

```text
pllm.testing.DistributionResult(kl_plain_to_workload: 'DistanceSummary', kl_workload_to_plain: 'DistanceSummary', tv: 'DistanceSummary', token_count: 'int', run_seconds: 'float', elapsed_seconds: 'float', failures: 'tuple[str, ...]')
```

KL units are nats. run_seconds includes generation and per-token diagnostics for both models;

## Stepwise Execution in Unit Tests

### `pllm.testing.compile_execution`

```text
pllm.testing.compile_execution(workload: 'Workload', facts: 'BackendCompileFacts', stream: 'torch.cuda.Stream | None' = None) -> 'StateExecution'
```

Compile `workload` against `facts` and admit its instance state, as the vLLM runner does on install.

Request state is admitted per request with `execution.admit(identities)`.

### `pllm.testing.backend_facts`

```text
pllm.testing.backend_facts(hidden_size: 'int', hidden: 'tuple[PackedHiddenResourceBinding, ...]' = (), *, device: 'str' = 'cpu', capabilities: 'tuple[str, ...]' = ..., pages: 'int' = 0, max_lineages: 'int' = 2, memory_bytes: 'int' = 10000, max_rows: 'int | None' = None, dtype: 'torch.dtype' = torch.float32, vocab_size: 'int' = 0, layer_count: 'int' = 0, targets: 'Mapping[Projection, tuple[int, int]]' = {}) -> 'BackendCompileFacts'
```

Facts for an eager in-process model, in place of what the vLLM runner probes.

`hidden` lists the taps the workload reads (see `hidden_binding`). `device` ("cpu" or "cuda") holds the
state pages; each state gets the versions its plan needs, or `pages` if a test holds more. `capabilities`
are the backend features plans may use; the default is everything a CPU simulation runs (overlays, AdamW,
custom forwards, token capture). `max_lineages` bounds
admitted requests, `memory_bytes` the state budget, and `max_rows` the packed rows per step (twice
`max_lineages` by default). `targets` maps overlay targets to their (input, output) widths; `vocab_size`
and `layer_count` are needed by workloads that read logits or layers.

### `pllm.testing.scheduled_step`

```text
pllm.testing.scheduled_step(identities: 'tuple[RequestIdentity, ...]', scheduled: 'list[int]', prompt: 'list[int]', computed: 'list[int]', hidden: 'Mapping[AttachmentHiddenResource, torch.Tensor]', *, step_id: 'int' = 0, operands: 'tuple[ProjectionOperands, ...]' = ()) -> 'StepInput'
```

Build a CPU step from scheduler counts, selecting only the runners' tapped rows.

Hidden inputs contain one value per packed token. Only completed prompt endings
and latest decode rows are retained, just as in HiddenTaps.prepare.

### `pllm.testing.step_input`

```text
pllm.testing.step_input(identities: 'Sequence[RequestIdentity]', hidden: 'Mapping[PackedHiddenResourceBinding, torch.Tensor] | None' = None, *, step_id: 'int' = 0, token_offset: 'int' = 0, tokens: "Sequence[Literal['prefill', 'decode']] | None" = None, sampler_order: 'Sequence[int] | None' = None, batch: 'HostBatch[torch.Tensor] | None' = None, operands: 'tuple[ProjectionOperands, ...]' = (), stream: 'torch.cuda.Stream | None' = None) -> 'StepInput'
```

One packed step: row i is the one token of request `identities[i]` at `token_offset`; it decodes unless
`tokens` says "prefill", which makes it the last token of the request's prompt.

`sampler_order` lists the packed row behind each sampler row (identity order by default; `()` for a
step without sampling). Hidden tensors are given per tap, one row per identity; CUDA tensors need the
`stream` they were produced on.

